decisions.thought:
Lead: 28% BRING: toxapex, 25% BRING: garchomp, 18% BRING: dragapult
Pick 2: 42% BRING: incineroar, 27% BRING: garchomp, 13% BRING: scizor
Pick 3: 37% BRING: garchomp, 30% BRING: scizor, 25% BRING: dragapult

Opponent has Toxapex (wall), Incineroar, Scizor, Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, Dragapult. I bring Incineroar (Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot), Garchomp (Mega for speed and power), and Gholdengo (strong special attacker, Life Orb). Lead Incineroar to cut their physical attackers. Plan: Fake Out or Intimidate first, then Garchomp Mega sweeps. Watch Dragapult's speed and Toxapex's poison/recovery.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Looking at the opponent's lineup against my own roster, I'm leaning toward Garchomp with mega evolution for speed and power, Incineroar for Intimidate and Fake Out support, and Corviknight for its bulk and utility against threats like Dragapult.

decisions.thought: 37% MOVE: toxicspikes, 32% MOVE: toxic, 12% SWITCH: garchomp

Plan: Toxapex is 4x weak to Ground, and Garchomp outspeeds it. Parting Shot brings Garchomp in to Earthquake it. Then Garchomp can Mega later. Watch for Toxapex's Toxic and Recover, Dragapult's speed, and Rotom-Wash's Electric attacks. Their Incineroar has Intimidate or Blaze, so expect Intimidate on switch-ins.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm thinking through turn 1, Incineroar vs Toxapex: Fake Out is usable here since it's the first turn, dealing neutral damage and causing flinch, while Toxapex's Intimidate would drop Incineroar's attack but its own low offensive stats mean it poses little immediate threat.

Flare Blitz isn't great here since Toxapex resists fire through its Water typing. I'm considering Parting Shot instead, dropping Toxapex's stats further while pivoting Incineroar out to bring in Garchomp, since Toxapex is quadruple weak to ground and Earthquake would hit it hard—though Toxapex's Toxic and Recover make it a slow war of attrition if I can't just blast through it.

decisions.thought: Toxapex is at -2 Atk and -1 SpA from Parting Shot and Intimidate. Garchomp outspeeds it and hits it 4x with Earthquake. Switching Garchomp in now. Plan: Earthquake Toxapex, consider Mega Garchomp later. Watch for Toxapex Toxic/Recover, Dragapult's speed, Rotom-Wash's Electric attacks, and Scizor's Bullet Punch or U-turn-style pivots.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: With Toxapex's stat drops in play, I need to switch out — Garchomp looks like the right call since it outspeeds Toxapex and hits it with a 4x Earthquake.

decisions.thought: 38% MOVE: toxic, 27% SWITCH: garchomp, 16% MOVE: toxicspikes

Turn 2: Toxapex is at -2 Atk and holds Toxic Spikes, so it's likely a Regenerator or Limber/Merciless wall. Garchomp outspeeds it and Earthquake is 4x effective. I'm keeping Mega Garchomp in reserve for a later threat (Dragapult or Rotom-Wash) rather than spending it on Toxapex. Opponent still has Incineroar, Scizor, Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, and Dragapult to come. Watch Dragapult's speed and Scizor's Bullet Punch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: With Toxapex down -2 Atk, I'm weighing whether Earthquake from Garchomp hits hard enough given Toxapex's tanky defenses, and considering if mega evolving would boost Garchomp's Attack enough to matter here.

decisions.thought: 39% SWITCH: garchomp, 25% MOVE: recover, 18% SWITCH: incineroar

Toxapex is at 40% after Leftovers. Garchomp outspeeds it and Earthquake did about 65% last turn, so a plain Earthquake should KO it without spending Mega. Keep Mega Garchomp for Dragapult or Rotom-Wash. Garchomp is poisoned (tox), so switch it out later to reset. Opponent still has Incineroar, Scizor, Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, Dragapult; Scizor and Dragapult are the main threats to watch. Gholdengo and Incineroar remain in reserve.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Toxapex is at 40% and already poisoned, so another Earthquake should finish it off since Garchomp outspeeds it regardless of the Attack drop. I'll stick with Earthquake again.

decisions.thought: 27% MOVE: dragonclaw [MEGA], 15% MOVE: earthquake [MEGA], 12% MOVE: stealthrock

Turn 4: Opposing Garchomp is at 50%. My Garchomp (152/185, poisoned) can likely KO it with a plain Earthquake, which is 2x on Dragon/Ground and 100% accurate. Keep Mega Garchomp in reserve for Dragapult or Rotom-Wash. Toxapex (Regenerator, Leftovers, Toxic Spikes) is back in the back. Scizor and Dragapult are the main threats; Dragapult may outspeed. Incineroar and Gholdengo are unused; Incineroar's Fake Out/Parting Shot can handle Scizor later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Garchomp is at 152/185 with toxic damage stacking, opponent's Garchomp down to 50%, and their Toxapex healed back to full via Regenerator on the switch. With speeds potentially tied around 169, I'm leaning toward hitting the opponent's Garchomp with Earthquake.

No need for the mega right now, I'll save it for later since Earthquake at full accuracy should do the job against their weakened Garchomp. I'll just go with Earthquake.

decisions.thought: 81% SWITCH: incineroar, 19% SWITCH: toxapex

Garchomp fainted (traded with their Mega Garchomp). Opponent has Toxapex (regenerating, Leftovers, Toxic Spikes, Toxic) and one more to come from Incineroar, Scizor, Rotom-Wash, or Dragapult. Our Toxic Spikes are up, so Incineroar would get poisoned on switch-in. Gholdengo is Steel, so it is immune to poison and Toxic Spikes, and it outspeeds Toxapex. Switch in Gholdengo, then use Nasty Plot or attack. Watch for Scizor's Bullet Punch and Dragapult's speed.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Both Garchomps are down now, and the opponent Mega Evolved with Sand Force while Toxapex sits fully healed on the field. They still have four more Pokémon to bring in. I'm weighing whether to send Incineroar or Gholdengo against Toxapex, since it's a sturdy wall on either side.

Gholdengo looks like the better pick since its Steel typing makes it immune to the Toxic Spikes and Toxapex's poison moves, plus it outspeeds and can set up Nasty Plot before breaking through with Make It Rain. Incineroar would just get poisoned on switch-in, so I'm going with Gholdengo.

decisions.thought: 30% SWITCH: toxapex, 25% MOVE: taunt, 18% MOVE: partingshot

Gholdengo (Life Orb, Atk -1 from Intimidate) is now active against Incineroar, which is at 100% with Sitrus Berry. Fire is super effective on Steel, so Flare Blitz is the main threat. Gholdengo outspeeds Incineroar (136 vs 72-123). Shadow Ball and Make It Rain are both resisted by Incineroar. Plan: Nasty Plot for a sweep if Gholdengo survives; otherwise switch to our Incineroar. Watch for Dragapult, Scizor's Bullet Punch, and Rotom-Wash. Toxic Spikes are up on our side; Gholdengo is immune to poison.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo is at -1 Attack from Intimidate, facing a full-health Incineroar now that Mega Garchomp fainted. I'm checking type matchups—Ghost actually hits Dark neutrally, not super effectively, so I need to reconsider Shadow Ball's value here.

More concerning is that Incineroar's Flare Blitz is super effective against Gholdengo's Steel typing and backed by high Attack, which could threaten a huge chunk of damage or even a knockout despite Gholdengo's decent bulk. Since Gholdengo outspeeds most Incineroar spreads, I'm weighing whether to attack first or play defensively given that speed advantage.

Weighing Shadow Ball's chip damage against Nasty Plot's upside — either way Incineroar's Flare Blitz likely threatens Gholdengo, but the +2 boost gives real sweep potential if it survives. I'll gamble on Nasty Plot.

decisions.thought: 55% SWITCH: incineroar, 14% MOVE: toxicspikes, 11% MOVE: toxic

Gholdengo (Good as Gold, so immune to Toxic and Toxic Spikes; Life Orb) is at +2 SpA against Toxapex, which can barely threaten it. Nasty Plot again to +4 is low-risk. Make It Rain is resisted by Toxapex, so Shadow Ball is the attack to use once the boosts are up. Watch for Incineroar's Flare Blitz, which hits Steel hard, and for Scizor and Dragapult switch-ins. Garchomp is down; Incineroar is in reserve.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing Gholdengo's options against Toxapex's tanky defenses — Shadow Ball hits neutrally since Toxapex is Poison/Water, while Make It Rain's Steel typing would be resisted.

Since Good as Gold makes Gholdengo immune to Toxic, another Nasty Plot feels relatively safe given Toxapex's weak offense, though I need to watch for a switch into Incineroar, which could threaten with Flare Blitz and an Intimidate drop.

decisions.thought: 60% MOVE: taunt, 17% SWITCH: toxapex, 10% MOVE: roar

Gholdengo is at +4 SpA with Life Orb and is faster than their Incineroar, but their Flare Blitz is super effective and could KO it (Atk -2 from Intimidate, so their hit may be slightly reduced). Shadow Ball is the best damage option now (roughly 55% to Incineroar, which has Sitrus). Expect a Flare Blitz next turn. If Gholdengo survives, Shadow Ball again. If it faints, bring in our Incineroar, which is poisoned by our Toxic Spikes only if it has no Poison typing. Toxapex, Scizor, Rotom-Wash and Dragapult are still unseen in reserve.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking matchup math: Gholdengo boosted on SpA but with lowered Attack from intimidate, facing Incineroar at full health, likely holding Sitrus Berry. Since Incineroar is Fire/Dark, Shadow Ball isn't particularly effective against it, so I need to reconsider the best move here.

Running the math, Shadow Ball at +4 against resisted Incineroar only lands around half its HP even with Life Orb, not a KO, while Make It Rain is worse due to the resist and SpA drop. Checking the risk of going to +6 with Nasty Plot instead: Incineroar's Flare Blitz is super effective on Gholdengo's Steel typing and could deal roughly 258+ damage with STAB and the type boost, which is a serious threat to weigh against the extra setup turn.

Weighing options now: staying in with Shadow Ball deals solid damage since Gholdengo moves first, but Incineroar's retaliation afterward is dangerous. Switching to my own Incineroar could apply Intimidate to soften that threat, though it exposes it to Flare Blitz and whatever hazards are already on my side.

decisions.thought: 75% SWITCH: toxapex, 14% MOVE: partingshot, 5% MOVE: roar

Gholdengo (+4 SpA, Life Orb, Good as Gold so immune to Taunt and Toxic) outspeeds the opposing Incineroar, which is at 9% and has no Sitrus left (item shown as unknown). Shadow Ball should KO it this turn. Next, expect Toxapex (regenerator, Toxic Spikes, Leftovers) or Scizor/Rotom-Wash/Dragapult. Keep Gholdengo for a sweep if possible; Incineroar's Flare Blitz is the main threat to it, and Protect is available as a stall tool.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar is at 9% HP with Taunt revealed, but Nasty Plot still shows as legal for my Gholdengo — that's because Good as Gold makes it immune to status moves like Taunt, so the taunt didn't actually land on it.

Incineroar's item is unknown, suggesting its Sitrus Berry already activated or was consumed, so there's nothing left to save it at 9% HP. Shadow Ball, even resisted by its Dark typing, should easily finish it off at +4 SpA with Gholdengo's speed advantage, so I'll go with that.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: 75% MOVE: partingshot, 17% MOVE: roar, 5% MOVE: willowisp

Opponent Incineroar is at 9% with its Sitrus Berry likely gone. Gholdengo (+4 SpA, Life Orb) outspeeds it and Shadow Ball should KO. Opponent has used Toxic Spikes, Toxic, Taunt, and Intimidate. Remaining unseen: Scizor, Rotom-Wash, Dragapult. Dragapult is the main threat to Gholdengo, so keep Incineroar in reserve. Gholdengo is immune to Toxic and Taunt via Good as Gold.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's at 9% with an unknown item, and Gholdengo outspeeds it. Since Incineroar is Fire/Dark, Shadow Ball won't be very effective against it since Dark resists Ghost.

Steel actually resists Fire, so Make It Rain is also not very effective here, same 0.5x as Shadow Ball. But either move should still finish Incineroar off given it's only at 9% of its HP, which is roughly 18 HP out of 170+ max - even a resisted hit from a +4 SpA boosted Gholdengo should overkill that easily.

I'll go with Shadow Ball since it has plenty of PP left and gets the job done.
